limitations: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE DATA: these numbers are not real observations.
Regions are approximate latitude/longitude boxes, not political borders; some boxes overlap.
Each grid cell is 2 x 2 degrees (about 220 km), so local details are not visible.

Temperature comes from a reanalysis (MERRA-2), evapotranspiration, runoff and soil moisture from a land surface model (GLDAS Noah), and precipitation from a satellite-gauge estimate (GPM IMERG); none is a direct measurement at every place, and the three sources differ in how they are made.

Trends are monotonic (Mann-Kendall, Sen's slope) over the stated period only; a change that rises and then falls can show as no significant trend, and a sudden jump (for example a change of satellite) can look like a trend.
Statistically significant does not mean large or important, and a trend says nothing about its cause.
Regional means average only the cells that pass the data requirement; land-only variables cover only the land part of a region.
Neighbouring grid cells are correlated, which makes the false discovery rate of a single map more variable than its 5% target.

methods.autocorrelation_note: Yue and Wang (2004) variance correction with an AR(1) model, floored at 1; recommended in trendkit docs/METHODS.md
methods.data_requirement: at least 10 years of valid months and at least 80% of months valid (trendkit)
methods.deseasonalizing: monthly climatology subtracted per cell and per regional series
methods.display_series: monthly anomalies and a trailing 12-month running mean (null until 12 valid months); no annual means are published because the last year is incomplete
methods.ranking: Sort by (1) tier: significant regional trend, then not significant, then insufficient data; (2) smaller regional p-value first; (3) larger |effect size| first, where effect size = trend per decade / standard deviation of the deseasonalized regional series.
methods.regional_mean: cos(latitude)-weighted mean of cells inside the box that pass the data requirement
methods.rounding: every number rounded to 4 significant digits
methods.trend_estimator: Sen's slope, reported per decade in the variable's units
